claims.text: Large language models are inherently statistical models due to their profound data dependency and stochastic generation processes.
Statistical insights are essential for handling variability and uncertainty in large language models.
The persistent black-box nature of large language models renders closed-form or purely mechanistic analyses generally intractable.
Statistical approaches are necessitated for large language model analysis due to their flexibility and effectiveness.
Statistical research concerning large language models will likely form a diverse mosaic of specialized topics rather than deriving from a single unifying theory.

evidence.description: The authors state that LLMs are inherently statistical models due to their profound data dependency and stochastic generation processes.
The paper notes statistical insights are naturally essential for handling variability and uncertainty in stochastic generation processes.
The paper argues that immense scale, architectural complexity, and empirical performance focus render closed-form or purely mechanistic analyses generally intractable.
The persistent black-box nature necessitates statistical approaches due to their flexibility and often demonstrated effectiveness.
The discussion suggests statistical research concerning LLMs will form a diverse mosaic of specialized topics rather than deriving from a single unifying theory.

limitations.text: Closed-form or purely mechanistic analyses of LLMs are generally intractable due to scale, architectural complexity, and empirical prioritization.
Statistical research on LLMs is unlikely to yield a single unifying theory.

future_work.text: Statistical research and timely engagement by the statistics community across areas including alignment, watermarking, uncertainty quantification, evaluation, and data mixture optimization.
